exercise.title: Sus2: the 2nd in place of the 3rd
exercise.why: A sus2 chord swaps the 3rd for the 2nd, so it is neither major nor minor until the 3rd comes back.

cells.text:
Tap {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} on the staff below: a D major chord, one note at a time. Now tap {{1}} {{2}} {{5}}: Dsus2, with the ringed {{2}} in place of {{3}}.
Go between the two until you can hum the note that moves.

Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Go from Dsus2 to D, where the 2nd rises to the 3rd, then from Dsus4 to D, where the 4th falls to it.
Keep going until you can tell the two sus chords apart by which way they move home.

Press the chord boxes of A below in the same way: Asus2 to A, then Asus4 to A.
When you change the key, the notes are new but sus2 still rises to the 3rd and sus4 still falls to it.
